bull.b: The recovery from prior losses to sustained profitability, alongside continued revenue growth and healthy operating margins, indicates stronger earnings capacity across the resort portfolio. This supports reinvestment and debt service.

Strong performance across Las Vegas, Boston and Macau reduces reliance on one property and shows the integrated-resort model can monetize gaming, lodging and amenities. Geographic and product breadth can support durable cash generation.

The amended concession provides regulatory clarity for Wynn Palace expansion and adds non-gaming capacity in Macau. New hotel, theater and event facilities could diversify revenue, strengthen the resort’s market position and support longer-term visitation.

bear.b: Very high debt and persistent negative equity leave Wynn financially dependent on debt-supported assets and ongoing cash generation. This reduces flexibility if resort performance weakens and raises the long-term burden of interest and refinancing.

Al Marjan’s cost increase and additional equity needs, combined with Macau expansion and concession commitments, require substantial capital before returns are realized. These demands could constrain debt reduction, buybacks and other uses of cash.

Profitability has improved but margins have compressed from earlier peaks while operating costs rise. Wage inflation, premium-service investment and variable gaming results could limit operating leverage and make earnings growth less consistent.
